_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel finally cooled off — $5.599/gal for the week of 8/31, down 5.3 cents after two straight ~20-cent jumps, so ease up on chasing the surcharge higher, but it's still $1.87 above last year and only ~21 cents off the 2022 record, so don't drop it either. Reefer just surged again as Yakima cherry season and produce lanes tighten — keep pushing refrigerated rates hard. Dry van stays the soft spot: linehaul's been sliding all August, so don't chase cheap freight, let it come to you.

_sourcing.status: ELEVENTH straight cycle with the WebFetch/curl egress block confirmed session-wide — see refreshBlockers. This cycle's headline finding: diesel REVERSED — the first down week after two straight ~20-cent jumps — $5.599/gal for the week ending 2026-08-31, down 5.3c from the prior confirmed $5.652 (arithmetic checks: 5.652-0.053=5.599), per EIA data corroborated across weeklydiesel.com's live DOE tracker and Logistics Management's 'National diesel average falls for the second time in the last eight weeks, reports EIA.' It did NOT break the June 2022 record ($5.810) — it's now ~21c off that mark (vs. ~16c off last cycle), still $1.865 above a year ago. asOf advanced to 2026-08-31 on this clean multi-source diesel confirmation. Trend downgraded from 'up' to 'flat' this cycle: signals are genuinely mixed, not uniformly up — diesel eased, dry van linehaul has been sliding all August ($2.32 on 8/3 to $2.25 on 8/17 to $2.19 on 8/26, all minus fuel, per DAT), while reefer 'surged' per a FleetOwner headline ($2.57/mi linehaul minus fuel for the week of ~9/3, up 13c vs the August average and +41c YoY) and flatbed load-to-truck tightened. Rather than force a single up/down call across contradictory equipment-level moves, 'flat' is the honest read. spotAllIn ($3.20), reefer modality ($3.33-3.38), dry van ($2.47-2.80), flatbed ($3.46-3.57), lanes, and commodityRates all carried forward unchanged this cycle — see per-field notes below for why each wasn't promoted.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE. $5.599/gal for the week ending 2026-08-31, down $0.053 w/w — the second down week in the last eight, per EIA, confirmed across weeklydiesel.com ('DOE Diesel Price This Week: $5.599 (week of August 31, 2026)') and Logistics Management, which explicitly cites EIA as the source. Checked for a fresher week-ending-9/7 reading: EIA's next release is 9/9, so 8/31 is the freshest published number as of this refresh (9/8). Diesel is easing, not breaking the 2022 record — now ~21c below the $5.810 all-time high, versus ~16c below it last cycle.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged, $3.20/mi (still dated week ending 2026-08-14 — no fresher blended all-in figure surfaced this cycle). Directional context found but not a clean absolute figure: DAT's own Aug 23-29 spot-market data (via AJOT) says reefer linehaul gained 6c while van and flatbed linehaul eased that week — consistent with a still-soft-to-flat blended spot market, but not convertible to a new all-in dollar figure without fabricating the fuel-surcharge component. Flagged needs-refresh.
_sourcing.modality: No modality reprices this cycle. Dry van: NOT promoted — last cycle's single-source $2.93 all-in reading (wk ending 8/14, CCJ/TheTrucker) resurfaced again this cycle but from the same underlying report, not a new independent source; a separate search initially returned a '$2.91 DAT Aug-18-Trendlines' claim, but a targeted follow-up search could not reproduce or trace that figure to a specific dated article — treating it as an unreliable AI-search-summary artifact and disregarding it rather than risk a fabricated promotion. Compounding the caution: DAT's own weekly linehaul series shows dry van actually declining through August ($2.32 to $2.25 to $2.19 minus fuel), which cuts against promoting the range upward. Carrying $2.47-2.80 forward, still flagged as needing a genuine second corroboration. Reefer: carried forward at $3.33-3.38 — this cycle's fresh reefer data point ($2.57/mi, linehaul minus fuel, FleetOwner) uses a different methodology (linehaul vs. the file's all-in figure) and can't be cleanly reconciled to a new all-in number without guessing the surcharge, so left unchanged; directionally consistent with 'surging,' i.e. still holding firm, not softening. Flatbed and LTL/Intermodal: no new data this cycle, unchanged.
_sourcing.commodityRates: Unchanged — no underlying modality line (dry van, reefer, flatbed) moved this cycle, so General Dry Freight (2.47), Frozen Seafood/Poultry (3.35), Fresh Produce (3.35), Coiled Steel (3.57), and High-Value Electronics (2.60) all carry forward as-is.
_sourcing.lanes: Carried forward, unchanged, for a SIXTH straight cycle. This cycle surfaced only percentage-based DAT blog commentary (Yakima-to-Northeast destination cities up 6-8% on cherry-season tightness) and one ambiguous fragment ('$1,000-$1,200 for certain produce movements' attributed to Atlanta) that doesn't specify miles or equipment clearly enough to convert to a trustworthy $/mi figure for a ~660-mile lane — not promoted. Still waiting on a clean, dated, absolute $/mi or $/load number from trade press or DAT Trendlines proper.
_sourcing.blurb: Rewritten this cycle to lead with diesel's reversal (first down week after two ~20-cent jumps) and the coaching not to over-correct the surcharge since it's still near-record; kept reefer's push-hard coaching since that story is still live (surging per FleetOwner); reframed dry van as the soft spot given the DAT linehaul decline data, coaching patience rather than chasing cheap freight.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Dry van's modality range is still the open item — needs a clean, independently-dated, all-in (not linehaul) reading distinct from the 8/14 CCJ/TheTrucker report before promoting past $2.47-2.80. Lanes need an absolute $/mi or $/load figure, not percentage deltas or ambiguous partial-load fragments. spotAllIn is now over three weeks stale (dated 8/14) and due for a refresh the moment a newer blended figure surfaces.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed. WebFetch to www.eia.gov returned 'EGRESS_BLOCKED' immediately. Raw curl to https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/, https://www.dat.com/, and the https://en.wikipedia.org/ control all returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' (exit code 56), with the agent-proxy logging all three as connect_rejected/organization policy. Confirms the block is unchanged across all ELEVEN weekly refreshes from 07-07 through 09-08. WebSearch remains the only working channel and delivered a clean diesel reversal this cycle ($5.599/gal, wk ending 8/31, down 5.3c, two independent EIA-citing sources) that supported advancing asOf to 2026-08-31 and downgrading trend from 'up' to 'flat' on genuinely mixed equipment-level signals (dry van linehaul sliding, reefer surging). Could not cleanly promote dry van's modality range, spotAllIn, or either lane this cycle — see per-field notes. Broader web-fetch access to eia.gov, dat.com/trendlines, or trade outlets directly (rather than relying on WebSearch's synthesized, occasionally untraceable summaries — see the dry-van '$2.91' artifact this cycle) would let those fields get the same clean-primary-source treatment diesel now consistently gets.
